title: Gaudí
objective: After this level you can describe Gaudí's curving buildings and mosaics in Barcelona.
summary: Gaudí designed the Sagrada Família with upside-down hanging models and columns that lean like trees, and covered curves in trencadís, a mosaic of broken tile.

cards.headline: Gaudí took over a Barcelona church in 1883. Its central tower rose in 2026.
cards.body: The church is the Sagrada Família. It occupied Antoni Gaudí until he died in 1926, when only one transept, with one of its towers, was finished. Builders completed its central Tower of Jesus Christ in February 2026, and finishing work goes on. How do you design a building that outlives you by a century? Gaudí started with string.

cards.headline: Design it upside down
cards.body: Remember Level 10's hanging chain? Gaudí turned it into a design tool. He hung networks of cords and loaded them with small bags of weight, standing in for the stone each arch would carry. A hanging cord is in pure tension. Turn its shape upside down and the forces become compression, running along the curve. He worked the method out for a church at the Colònia Güell, near Barcelona, then carried it into the Sagrada Família.

mascot.line: Gravity did the sums. Gaudí just had to hold the drawing upside down.

cards.headline: Columns that lean like trees
cards.body: Level 4's arches push outward at their feet, a diagonal thrust that massive supports must resist. Gaudí wanted his buildings to stand without buttresses propping them from outside, the way a tree stands. So his piers and columns tilt, leaning along the diagonal thrust they carry. Inside the Sagrada Família they rise like a forest of twisting stone trunks. The lean isn't a wobble. It's the force, made visible.

cards.fact: Gaudí covered his curves in broken tile.
cards.context: The technique is called trencadís: a mosaic of broken ceramic pieces. Small pieces can follow a curved surface that flat, whole tiles can't. Its best-known showcase is the long, undulating bench in Park Güell, glittering with color. UNESCO lists seven of Gaudí's works in and near Barcelona as World Heritage, first inscribed in 1984 and extended in 2005.

cards.headline: Gaudí: mapped
learned: Sagrada Família: Gaudí's life's work from 1883
Hanging models flipped into arches in compression
Tilted columns stand like trees, with no outside buttresses
Trencadís: broken tile that hugs curves

questions.prompt: What is trencadís, the finish on Park Güell's undulating bench?

options.label: A mosaic of broken ceramic tile pieces
Carved blocks of local sandstone
options.rationale: Trencadís is a mosaic, not carved stone.

options.label: Sheets of colored glass set in lead
Painted plaster over brick
options.rationale: The color comes from broken tile, not paint.

questions.explanation: Trencadís is a mosaic of broken ceramic pieces; small pieces can follow curved surfaces like Park Güell's bench.

questions.prompt: Why do many of Gaudí's columns in the Sagrada Família tilt instead of standing straight?

options.label: To make the church look older than it is
options.rationale: The tilt is structural, not a style of aging.

options.label: Because the ground beneath them sank
options.rationale: The lean was designed from the start.

options.label: To leave room for the mosaic panels
options.rationale: The mosaics are not the reason.

options.label: They lean along the diagonal thrust they carry

questions.explanation: Gaudí tilted his piers and columns along the diagonal thrusts they carry, so the building could stand without outside buttresses, like a tree.

questions.prompt: Gaudí's weighted-cord models put Level 10's hanging-chain idea to work. What is that idea?

options.label: An arch needs one keystone heavier than the rest
options.rationale: The idea is about the shape of the curve.

options.label: A hanging shape in tension, flipped, stands as an arch in compression
Stone is strongest when it is stretched
A dome's rim is squeezed all the way around

questions.explanation: A hanging chain or cord is in tension along its curve; turned upside down, the same shape is an arch in compression.
